Warnings and errors the package raises

Source: R/spatialkit-topics.R
spatialkit-conditions.Rd

Every condition class the package raises, with the functions that raise it, what it means, what to do and the fields it carries. Each class can be caught by name.

Catching a condition by class

Each condition below is an R warning or error whose class vector starts with the class named, followed by "warning" or "error" and "condition". A handler named after the class catches it without matching the message, and reads its fields with $:


w <- tryCatch(determine_optimal_levels(pts),
              spatialkit_no_elbow = function(w) w)
w$k

withCallingHandlers() with invokeRestart("muffleWarning"), or suppressWarnings(expr, classes = ), lets the call finish and drops the warning. options(warn = 2) turns every warning into an error.

Some warnings and errors carry no class of the package's own, such as the refusal of an argument of the wrong type. Catch those with warning = or error =.

Warnings and log lines

The package also writes a log through logger: a trace in a temporary file, and a console echo of every line at the WARN level and above. A log line is not an R condition. tryCatch(warning = ) does not catch it, and suppressWarnings() does not silence it. Where a help page says a function raises a warning, it means an R warning; where it says the function logs one, it means a log line. spatialkit_quiet() turns the console echo off.

The package writes a classed warning to the log as well as raising it, so a warning muffled by a handler still prints its log line until the echo is turned off.

Condition classes

Each entry gives the class, the functions that raise it, what it means and what to do, and then the fields a handler reads with $. Each is a warning unless marked as an error. An entry without fields is a condition that carries only its message.

  • spatialkit_aoa_zero_threshold. Raised by area_of_applicability() with folds. The dissimilarity threshold is 0: held-out rows have exact copies on the training side of their fold. Use folds that keep copies together, such as make_folds(method = "leave_location_out", group_var = ).

  • spatialkit_bound_chosen. Raised by get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans() and build_tessellation(), given a profile or a selection as the count. The optimum sits on a bound of the ladder, so a bound of the ladder set the count. Read edge in the select_resolution() result; resolution_profile() describes the bounds. Fields: edge, criterion and n.

  • spatialkit_cells_degenerate (error; a warning from ensure_stable_poly_id()). Raised by build_tessellation(), create_voronoi_polygons(), create_grid_polygons(), clip_target_for(), get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_random(), make_folds(), assign_features_to_polygons(), summarize_by_cell(), cell_values_at() and ensure_stable_poly_id(). s2 refuses a cell or a boundary row in lon/lat even after repair, or a boundary in a geographic CRS has a vertex beyond latitude 90. From ensure_stable_poly_id(): the repair left a row with no polygon. Transform the layer to a projected CRS; for a latitude beyond 90, check its CRS. Fields: rows, n and reasons; the error also carries parent, repaired and s2_forced, and some steps add site, cause or features_rows.

  • spatialkit_cells_differ. Raised by summarize_by_cell(). The rows or cells given are not those the count was scored on; what says which check differs. Summarise the layer the count was chosen on, assigned to the cells built from that selection. Fields: what, scored and found, and field for the count record.

  • spatialkit_constant_predictor. Raised by prep_model_data(), and so by every fitter and cv_*() function. A predictor takes one value in every row kept, so its coefficient cannot be told from the intercept. Drop it from predictor_vars.

  • spatialkit_constant_response. Raised by resolution_profile(). The scored variable is constant to within rounding, so cp, moran_i and moran_z are NA at every level. Check the response. With predictor_vars, a response the predictors fit exactly leaves constant residuals. Fields: n.

  • spatialkit_convergence. Raised by fit_bayesian_spatial_model(), cv_bayes() and cv_spatial(). The sampler's diagnostics fail (divergent transitions, R-hat, effective sample size or E-BFMI), and convergence_ok is FALSE. Raise adapt_delta for divergent transitions; run more iterations for R-hat and effective sample size. Fields: failed, and from cross-validation also folds and fold_messages.

  • spatialkit_cp_noise. Raised by resolution_profile(). cp does not take the variogram's nugget as it stands, or has no noise variance and is NA at every level. Read attr(, "cp_noise") for the variance cp used and its source. Fields: source, value, level, cap, uncapped_source and uncapped_value.

  • spatialkit_deff_fallback. Raised by summarize_by_cell(). The design effect requested was not the one applied: a "variogram" request fell back to Kish's, or a number given was refused. Read the deff_method column; deff_method == "variogram" keeps the rows the variogram corrected. Fields, for a "variogram" request: requested and used.

  • spatialkit_deff_no_structure. Raised by summarize_by_cell(). The variogram of the response found no spatial structure, so the predictor columns named get a design effect of 1 from a verdict about the response. Use deff = "kish" to give each predictor its own ICC. Fields: columns and reason.

  • spatialkit_diagnostic_criterion (error). Raised by select_resolution(). criterion = "moran_z" was asked for without diagnostic = TRUE. moran_z is a diagnostic of the cell means, which select_resolution() reads only under diagnostic = TRUE. Pass diagnostic = TRUE, or choose another criterion.

  • spatialkit_diagnostic_ranking. Raised by determine_optimal_levels() with criterion = "morans_i". The candidates are ranked by Moran's z of the cell means, a diagnostic of the cells. Use criterion = "geometric", or resolution_profile() when the response should drive the count. Fields: k, criterion, first_computable and window.

  • spatialkit_empty_cells. Raised by resolution_profile(), get_voronoi_seeds() and voronoi_seeds_kmeans() with partition = "density". A centre holds no point, so fewer cells are occupied than the count. It happens at high counts, mostly from random starts. k-means++ starts (init = "kmeans++") leave a cell empty less often. Fields: level and empty.

  • spatialkit_estimate_mismatch. Raised by summarize_by_cell(). The summary reports another cell value than the count was chosen for: plain means against pooled values, or the reverse. Report the value the count was chosen for, or choose the count for the value you report. Fields: chosen_for, reported, rule and cells.

  • spatialkit_features_degenerate (error). Raised by coerce_to_points(), prep_model_data(), assign_features_to_polygons() and cell_values_at(). s2 refuses a polygon of the features in lon/lat, GEOS puts the centroid of an invalid feature outside it, or a temporary projection leaves a line empty. Transform the features to a projected CRS, choose another mode in coerce_to_points(), or repair them with sf::st_make_valid(). Fields: rows, n, reasons, parent, repaired and s2_forced, and some steps add site, crs or auto_helps.

  • spatialkit_few_residuals. Raised by summarize_by_cell() with obs_level. Fewer than five residuals are expected beyond each end of the interval (at 0.90, fewer than 100 residuals), so its ends are unstable. Ask for a lower obs_level, which needs fewer residuals. Fields: columns, needed, level and n.

  • spatialkit_fold_args_ignored. Raised by cv_spatial(), cv_rf(), cv_gwr(), cv_bayes() and compare_models_cv(). block_size or auto_range = TRUE was given beside folds, which leaves them nothing to size. Drop them, or leave out folds so the function builds the blocks.

  • spatialkit_gp_adequacy. Raised by fit_bayesian_spatial_model(), cv_bayes() and cv_spatial(). The basis of the Bayesian GP is too coarse: the posterior asks for a shorter length-scale than it resolves, or the residuals are autocorrelated at short range. Follow the message: a finer basis (gp_k, gp_resolution) or, at its cap, kriging or a model of cell means. Fields, from cross-validation: folds and fold_messages.

  • spatialkit_gp_basis_size. Raised by fit_bayesian_spatial_model(), cv_bayes() and cv_spatial(). Fewer than one row per ten basis functions, so most basis weights are set by their prior. A smaller gp_k is cheaper and resolves less; with this few rows kriging fits the same kind of model. Fields, from cross-validation: folds and fold_messages.

  • spatialkit_gp_resolution. Raised by fit_bayesian_spatial_model(), cv_bayes() and cv_spatial(). A variogram fitted before compiling puts the response's range below what the basis resolves, and the response's autocorrelation agrees. The check after sampling tests this estimate. The message gives the basis size that would resolve the range. Fields, from cross-validation: folds and fold_messages.

  • spatialkit_gwr_extrapolation. Raised by predict.gwr_fit(), predict_surface(), cv_gwr(), cv_spatial(), cv_block_size_sweep() and select_features_forward(). New locations lie beyond the reach of the widest kernel; they are predicted and counted. Where extrapolation is intended, use suppressWarnings(expr, classes = "spatialkit_gwr_extrapolation"). Fields: n_far, n, reach, reach_text, nearest and calls.

  • spatialkit_gwr_not_estimable. Raised by predict.gwr_fit(), predict_surface(), cv_gwr(), cv_spatial(), cv_block_size_sweep() and select_features_forward(). The local regression at a new location cannot be estimated, so its prediction is NA. predict.gwr_fit() says when a window cannot be estimated. Fields: n_na, n, n_empty, bw_text and calls.

  • spatialkit_gwr_rank_deficient. Raised by fit_gwr_model(). Some local windows have deficient rank, and their coefficients are NA; the fitted values are returned. Where many windows hold a predictor constant, fit it as one global coefficient (a mixed GWR, as GWmodel::gwr.mixed() fits).

  • spatialkit_gwr_repeated_locations. Raised by fit_gwr_model() and gwr_model_selection(). Rows share coordinates. AICc counts them as independent, so a bandwidth left to the search (bandwidth = NULL) is chosen by leave-one-location-out error, and the AICc gaps between models make what a predictor adds look larger than it is. Read "Observations that share a location" in fit_gwr_model().

  • spatialkit_icc_unavailable. Raised by summarize_by_cell(). A column's Kish ICC cannot be estimated, so its standard errors and intervals are NA in cells of two or more observations. attr(, "icc")$reason says why. Fields: columns and reason.

  • spatialkit_k_reduced. Raised by make_folds(), and the functions that build folds with it. Fewer folds were made than asked for. Read k in the result; the message gives the reason and a setting that works. Fields: k_requested and k.

  • spatialkit_knndm_short_of_target. Raised by make_folds() with method = "knndm". The held-out points sit closer to their training data than the prediction points do, so the cross-validated error tends to read low. Use fewer folds; each then holds out a larger part of the layer. Fields: held_out_mean and target_mean.

  • spatialkit_ladder_unused. Raised by resolution_profile(). A numeric obs_per_cell sets the ladder, so the n_levels, min_cell_n, sample_n or range_floor = TRUE also given are not read. Pass obs_per_cell or those arguments, not both. Fields: unused and obs_per_cell.

  • spatialkit_lat_beyond_90. Raised by coerce_to_points() and ensure_stable_poly_id(). Rows of a layer in a geographic CRS have a vertex at a latitude beyond 90, which is no place on the Earth. coerce_to_points() gives them an empty point; ensure_stable_poly_id() keys them as empty polygons and returns them as they came. Check the layer's CRS and the order of its coordinates. Fields: rows and n.

  • spatialkit_moran_skipped. Raised by resolution_profile(). A level has more than 5,000 cells holding a scored row while FNN cannot be loaded or Matrix is not installed, so moran_i and moran_z are NA there. Install Matrix, or reinstall FNN. Fields: limit, levels and missing.

  • spatialkit_new_levels. Raised by predict.bayesian_fit(). Rows carry a level of a categorical predictor that the model was not fitted with, so their predictions are NA. The warning names the predictor, the levels and the number of rows.

  • spatialkit_nndm_out_of_reach. Raised by make_folds() with method = "nndm" or "knndm". The prediction points sit nearer to the data than any fold can hold a point out, so the cross-validated error is pessimistic for them. No fold setting closes the gap; read the score as an upper bound on the error at those points. Fields: deficit, tolerance and separated.

  • spatialkit_no_cover. Raised by build_tessellation() and create_voronoi_polygons(). Seeds came with neither a boundary nor a cover, so their cells cover only the seeds' own hull. Pass the study area as boundary, or the observations as cover.

  • spatialkit_no_default_criterion (error). Raised by get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans() and build_tessellation(). A profile passed as the count has cp, the criterion a profile is read by, NA at every level while another criterion is finite. Pass select_resolution(profile, criterion = ) with a finite criterion, or a number.

  • spatialkit_no_elbow (an error under on_no_elbow = "error"). Raised by determine_optimal_levels(). The WSS curve has no elbow, or the ladder is too short to show one, so the count it gives is set by the ladder. Choose the count on other grounds, such as resolution_profile() with a response. Fields: k, sag and structured.

  • spatialkit_no_scored_rows. Raised by resolution_profile(). No row of the selection half has a response (select_on = "split"), or no row has a response and every predictor, so the columns that read those rows are NA at every level. reason says which; check where the rows with a response and every predictor lie. Fields: reason, n, selection, n_response and column.

  • spatialkit_no_structure. Raised by get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans(), build_tessellation() and summarize_by_cell() with estimate = "pooled". One cell for the whole layer does as well (structured is FALSE), so the cell values say little that one mean does not. The call goes on with the count. The message says which test failed, and whether a size set the count; see "Pooled values" in summarize_by_cell(). Fields: criterion, n and one_cell, and from summarize_by_cell() also columns, estimate, loo, structure_p and beats.

  • spatialkit_nonfinite. Raised by summarize_by_cell(). Inf or -Inf in a response or predictor column is treated as missing in every statistic of that column; n still counts the row. The warning names the columns and gives the rows and cells affected. Fields: n and columns.

  • spatialkit_not_converged. Raised by resolution_profile(), get_voronoi_seeds() and voronoi_seeds_kmeans(). The start kept was cut off at the iteration limit, so a longer run could still move points between cells. Raise iter_max (kmeans_iter in get_voronoi_seeds()). Fields: level, iter and iter_max.

  • spatialkit_not_supported. Raised by resolution_profile(). supported is FALSE: the range floor exceeds the ceiling, fewer than two cells meet min_cell_n, or the points sit on one location. attr(x, "bounds") gives the floor, the ceiling and ceiling_from. Fields: reason, n and min_cell_n, and obs_per_cell for a ladder of sizes.

  • spatialkit_partition_unused. Raised by get_voronoi_seeds() and voronoi_seeds_kmeans(). Given a profile or a selection, the call also named a partition, init or density setting other than the profile's; the scored centres are returned. Pass the count as a number (n = sel$best) for a fresh k-means. Fields: kind and init.

  • spatialkit_pool_degenerate. Raised by summarize_by_cell() with estimate = "pooled". The pooled values carry no pooling: one cell, no spread inside any cell, or no signal between cells. reason says which case applies. Fields: reason and columns, with n, constant or sigma2 by case.

  • spatialkit_pool_few_cells. Raised by summarize_by_cell() with estimate = "pooled". The column has 2 to 9 cells, so each target is the mean of all the other cells, and a pooled value can land on the far side of the overall mean from its plain mean. With 10 cells or more each target is the mean of the observations in the 8 nearest cells. Fields: columns, cells and own_weight.

  • spatialkit_pool_few_df. Raised by summarize_by_cell() with estimate = "pooled". The spread inside the cells (sigma2), which every own weight rests on, comes from fewer than 30 values beyond one per cell. Fewer cells leave more values beyond one per cell. Fields: columns, needed, df, n and cells.

  • spatialkit_pool_rows_skipped. Raised by summarize_by_cell() with estimate = "pooled". Rows with a value and a cell have no location; they count in n and the plain columns and take no part in the pooled ones. See "Rows without a location" in spatialkit-geometry. Fields: n, cells and columns.

  • spatialkit_pool_unavailable. Raised by summarize_by_cell() with estimate = "pooled" and resolution_profile() with an estimate. The pooled columns (in a profile, loo, loo_se and own_weight) are NA; reason says why. The plain columns are returned. For "values out of range", divide the column by a power of ten; for "work limit", see spatialkit-options. Fields: reason and columns, with n and cells, or work, limit and cells, by reason.

  • spatialkit_predict_failed. Raised by predict.bayesian_fit(). The posterior draw failed, and every prediction is NA. The message gives the cause.

  • spatialkit_repeated_locations. Raised by summarize_by_cell() with obs_level and resolution_profile() with an estimate. Rows share a location, so the interval or loo describes a further observation at a place already observed. Fields: n, the rows that share a location, and total, the rows read, with columns from summarize_by_cell() or column from resolution_profile().

  • spatialkit_replicate_var_above_nugget. Raised by kriging_adequacy(). The replicates at one location vary between visits more than the variogram's nugget allows; their variance is used as it is. Refit the variogram with a nugget of at least the replicate variance. Fields: within_var and nugget.

  • spatialkit_response_ceiling. Raised by resolution_profile(). Rows that are not scored (no response, or a predictor missing) lowered the ceiling on the count. The message names the bound in force. Fields: n, n_response, ceiling, ceiling_from, n_sample and n_scored.

  • spatialkit_response_imprecise. Raised by prep_model_data(), and so by every fitter and cv_*() function, and by estimate_sac_range(), kriging_adequacy() and select_features_forward(). The response lies so far from zero that doubles there are spaced more than a millionth of its standard deviation apart, and every mean is rounded to that spacing. Subtract a constant from the response first. Fields: spacing and spread.

  • spatialkit_response_scale. Raised by fit_bayesian_spatial_model(). prior sets a prior on the response's scale, so a response far from zero, or with a standard deviation far from 1, is handed to brms as it is. See "The response's centre and scale" in fit_bayesian_spatial_model().

  • spatialkit_rows_dropped. Raised by prep_model_data(), and so by every fitter and cv_*() function, and by gp_lengthscale_bounds(). Rows were dropped for a missing or non-finite value or for having no location. The message gives the counts and how far the dropped rows' mean response sits from the kept rows'. When that difference is large, the fit is biased towards the complete rows. Fields, from gp_lengthscale_bounds(): n and which.

  • spatialkit_rows_unplaced. Raised by ensure_projected(), harmonize_crs(), plot_tessellation_map(), and the other functions that move a layer into another CRS. The target CRS cannot place a row in full, so the row comes back empty or without those vertices. Correct or drop those rows. Fields: rows and n.

  • spatialkit_sd_overflow. Raised by summarize_by_cell(). A cell's standard deviation is beyond the largest double, so its ..sd_* is Inf and its standard errors and interval are NA. Divide the column by a power of ten. Fields: columns and cells.

  • spatialkit_size_not_reached. Raised by resolution_profile(), select_resolution() and get_voronoi_seeds(). A size does not give the count it asks for (fewer than two cells, or more than k-means can place), and the nearest level is used. Fields: obs_per_cell, wanted and used, the two counts, and reason.

  • spatialkit_surface_point_off. Raised by coerce_to_points(). The point GEOS takes on a lon/lat polygon spanning more than 180 degrees of longitude does not lie on it read on the sphere, and that point is kept. Transform the layer to a projected CRS that holds the polygon, and call again. Fields: rows.

  • spatialkit_ties_unresolved. Raised by assign_features_to_polygons(). The tie_break rule names no polygon for some features, since the polygons are equal on every key; those features get NA. They are kept or dropped as keep_unassigned says. Fields: n and total.

  • spatialkit_unassigned. Raised by assign_features_to_polygons(), build_tessellation() and create_voronoi_polygons(). Features fall inside no polygon, or points or seeds lie outside every cell. Give the cells a boundary or cover that reaches the data; keep_unassigned = TRUE keeps such features with NA. Fields: n and total.

  • spatialkit_variogram_unusable. Raised by resolution_profile(). The variogram gives no usable range, so reliability is NA. reason gives the rejected_reason of estimate_sac_range(). Fields: reason, converged, nugget and nugget_used.

  • spatialkit_work_limit (error). Raised by resolution_profile() and cell_values_at(). A search or a fit would make more comparisons than an option allows. The message says what to change; see spatialkit-options. Fields: work, limit and what, and for a fit also kind, init, nstart and fnn.

  • spatialkit_xy_imprecise. Raised by assign_features_to_polygons(), build_tessellation(), create_voronoi_polygons(), create_grid_polygons(), clip_target_for(), make_folds(), estimate_sac_range(), fit_gwr_model() and residual_morans_i(). The coordinates lie so far from the origin of their CRS that doubles there are spaced more than a millionth of the extent apart, or a distance lies past a tie by less than that rounding. The call runs on the rounded coordinates. Subtract a constant from the coordinates; see "Coordinates far from the origin" in spatialkit-geometry. Fields: spacing, and extent or distance.

  • spatialkit_xy_imprecise_error (error). Raised by clip_target_for(). At that rounding the buffer comes back empty or with no area. Shift the points nearer the origin, or pass boundary.

  • spatialkit_zm_dropped. Raised by ensure_projected(), harmonize_crs(), coerce_to_points(), assign_features_to_polygons(), get_voronoi_seeds(), ensure_stable_poly_id(), predict_surface() and area_of_applicability(). A layer that mixes XY and XYZ (or XYM) geometries came back in XY, or coerce_to_points() reduced geometries that carry M in x and y. See "Mixed dimensions, Z and M" in spatialkit-geometry. Fields: rows, the rows that carried Z or M.

See also

spatialkit_quiet() for the console log, spatialkit-options for the work limits, spatialkit-geometry for the rules behind the geometry classes, and vignette("troubleshooting", package = "spatialkit") for the messages met most often.

Other options and caches: clear_fitted_cache(), clear_grid_cache(), spatialkit-options, spatialkit_quiet()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
# Points spread evenly have no elbow.
pts <- st_as_sf(data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(200, 0, 100),
                           y = 5e6 + runif(200, 0, 100)),
                coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)

# Catch the warning by its class and read its fields.
w <- tryCatch(determine_optimal_levels(pts, max_levels = 6),
              spatialkit_no_elbow = function(w) w)
class(w)
#> [1] "spatialkit_no_elbow" "warning"             "condition"          
w$k
#> [1] 3

# Let the call finish without the warning; the log line still prints
# until the console echo is off.
old <- spatialkit_quiet()
k <- suppressWarnings(determine_optimal_levels(pts, max_levels = 6),
                      classes = "spatialkit_no_elbow")
spatialkit_quiet(old)
k
#> [1] NA
#> attr(,"structured")
#> [1] FALSE
#> attr(,"sag")
#> [1] 0
